role: Continuing own independent primary-source adjudicator; not a new fresh vote.
scope: Narrow literal-question dependency check using original 2008 rulebook and applicable official 2018 FAQ. No source-conflict adjudication, global bank assessment, score, or PASS.
literal_question: Before compensation starts, may you legally play a reinforcement to remove it from your hand? Once Hacker has targeted your hand, may you then dump it, and what kinds of effects can interrupt the hand-targeting action?
supplied_expected_record: Legal cards may be played in their ordinary timing windows before compensation begins.
Once Hacker targets the hand, the earlier reinforcement opportunity has passed; ordinary card play cannot interrupt the hand-targeting effect.
Only a Zap or a power/effect explicitly permitting interruption can interrupt it.
supplied_contextual_qualifier: Only while the normal timing window is open; no permission during compensation.

answer.first_clause: Yes, if the reinforcement is otherwise legally playable and its normal play opportunity is still open before compensation begins. Merely being before compensation does not grant a new play window or settle every other legality requirement.
answer.second_clause: No. You cannot wait for Hacker to target your hand and then dump the reinforcement; the earlier opportunity to affect encounter totals has passed.
answer.third_clause: Only a Zap or a power/effect specifically permitting interruption can interrupt the hand-targeting effect. Ordinary card play cannot interrupt it.

source_legal_facts.locator: 2008 rulebook p.13, Reinforcement Cards; extract lines 1034–1046
source_legal_facts.quote:
Instead, during the Reveal
Phase, after encounter cards are revealed, the offense, defense,
and any allies may play reinforcement cards on either side of
the encounter
source_legal_facts.fact: The ordinary reinforcement opportunity is a defined Reveal-phase opportunity with participating roles. It is not any arbitrary moment before compensation.

source_legal_facts.locator: 2008 rulebook p.13, Reinforcement Cards; extract lines 1043–1046
source_legal_facts.quote:
Players may continue playing reinforcements in
response to other reinforcements until all players pass. Once all
players have passed on the opportunity to play further rein-
forcements, the encounter is resolved with the new totals.
source_legal_facts.fact: The reinforcement opportunity closes before resolution of the encounter under these ordinary timing instructions.

source_legal_facts.locator: 2008 rulebook p.10, attack versus negotiate; extract lines 780–786, and p.11 Compensation, lines 887–895
source_legal_facts.quote:
When one player plays a negotiate and his opponent plays an
attack card, the player who played the negotiate card gets to
collect compensation.
source_legal_facts.fact: Ordinary compensation is distinct from computing attack totals and is described in Resolution. This ordinary source setting does not by itself resolve the conflicting FAQ reinforcement-type permissions.

source_legal_facts.locator: Official FAQ p.3; extract lines 238–252, particularly 241–246
source_legal_facts.quote:
You are free to use any cards that may be 
legally played before compensation begins to be collected. So, you 
could play a reinforcement card to get it out of your hand before 
compensation is taken, for instance.
source_legal_facts.fact: The source itself predicates the pre-compensation example on cards that may legally be played. It does not create blanket legality from the words before compensation.

source_legal_facts.quote:
However, once the 
opportunity to play such cards has passed and compensation 
begins, then it is too late. For example, you cannot wait to see if 
Hacker is going to target you before deciding whether to “dump” 
your reinforcement cards, because the time to affect encounter 
totals has already passed.
source_legal_facts.fact: The exact Hacker reinforcement-dumping example answers the late-play portion explicitly, independently of deciding which revealed card combinations permit a reinforcement in the earlier window.

source_legal_facts.quote:
Once an effect targets your hand, 
nothing can interrupt that effect except a Zap or some other 
power or effect that specifically lets you interrupt it.
source_legal_facts.fact: The permitted exception class for interruption is explicit.

source_legal_facts.quote:
Other than playing a Zap of some kind, or an effect that 
specifically allows you to interrupt an action, no. You must 
complete an effect before executing another one.
source_legal_facts.fact: The immediately preceding generic interruption answer agrees with the hand-targeting rule.

unresolved_primary_conflict.p3_quote:
Yes, any player involved in the encounter may play a 
reinforcement on either side, regardless of what type of encounter 
cards were revealed.
unresolved_primary_conflict.p3_question_scope: The preceding question explicitly includes attack versus negotiate and both negotiates.
unresolved_primary_conflict.p4_quote:
Q: Can you play a reinforcement card on a negotiate?
A: No.
unresolved_primary_conflict.status: Conflict recorded, not resolved, ranked, harmonized, or assigned to a particular side or card-type scenario.
unresolved_primary_conflict.consequence: These statements can affect whether a concrete reinforcement play involving a negotiate is otherwise legal. This adjudication supplies no such concrete legality verdict.

question_scope_interpretation.type: Interpretation of the supplied literal question and its supplied contextual qualifier, separate from published legal facts.
reasoning: The first clause asks about an opportunity before compensation, not a supplied revealed-card combination. It can be fully answered as yes only while otherwise legal in the normal window; the task explicitly supplies that qualifier.
The primary FAQ uses the same example and the same legally-playable qualification. Carrying that qualification into the answer preserves rather than resolves its legality dependencies.
No role, revealed attack/negotiate combination, exact earlier instant, or power is supplied for a concrete legality ruling. None is invented.
The later clauses ask about the closed timing opportunity and interruption exceptions. Their published answers do not require choosing between the two card-type permission statements.

Ordinary compensation’s attack/negotiate origin is not silently converted into a concrete reinforcement-eligibility test in the first clause. Doing that would broaden this conditional timing question into the very separate disputed card-type question.
question_scope_interpretation.logical_form: If otherwise legally playable AND the ordinary play opportunity remains open AND compensation has not begun, the player may play the card. After hand-targeting begins, ordinary play cannot interrupt; a specific allowed interruption is required.
question_scope_interpretation.what_is_not_proved: This conditional does not establish that any arbitrary card or every reinforcement in every compensation-producing encounter has a legal earlier play opportunity.
question_scope_interpretation.why_first_clause_does_not_necessarily_fo: Nothing in the literal clause demands an unconditional yes across all revealed-card combinations. The contextual qualifier explicitly limits the answer to otherwise legal normal-window play. The legality condition may remain a condition without enumerating or settling its disputed applications.

dependency_boundary.safe_complete_requested_answer: The three timing and interruption propositions, with their stated legal-window condition, are fully supported.
would_require_more_or_conflict_resolutio: An unconditional yes merely because compensation has not started.
A ruling that an attack-versus-negotiate or both-negotiate encounter definitely permits or forbids a particular earlier reinforcement play.
An instruction to play the reinforcement during compensation, at hand targeting, or after the ordinary opportunity has closed.
dependency_boundary.not_a_placeholder: The answer states the requested timing rule affirmatively and answers the Hacker and interruption clauses explicitly. It does not defer any of those timing conclusions.
dependency_boundary.source_conflict_remains: Yes, as to underlying card-type eligibility; no conflict resolution is attempted here.

publication_status.direct_published: The legal-play-before-compensation condition, Hacker too-late example, and specific interruption exceptions are stated expressly in the FAQ.
publication_status.derived_scope_judgment: Treating those three statements as a complete answer to the supplied Q074 with its normal-window qualifier is this adjudicator’s narrow literal-scope interpretation; Q074 is not asserted to be a published official question identifier.

confidence: High for conditional timing adequacy and the explicit Hacker/interruption answers; no confidence verdict is assigned to the unresolved card-type conflict.
limitations: No scenario facts beyond those supplied are inferred.
No unrestricted pre-compensation reinforcement permission is endorsed.
No underlying conflict is resolved or treated as absent.
